report.source_text: Meningitis started occurring more frequently and was accompanied by sudden brownish urine and occasionally by altered consciousness, which lasted for several days. At the age of 68, the patient developed severe haemolysis. Haemoglobin declined to 8.2 g/dL and lactate dehydrogenase elevated up to 3004 IU/L. He also developed acute renal failure because of the deposition of haemosiderin in renal tubules. Serum creatinine increased from 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL. He required temporary haemodialysis for a month until his condition improved.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) with recurrent aseptic meningitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with 121 episodes of recurrent aseptic meningitis over 18 years, beginning at age 53. He had a prior history of recurrent urticaria and arthralgia since age 30. Extensive initial workup ruled out infectious etiologies (negative bacterial, fungal, mycobacterial cultures; negative PCR for herpesviruses and enteroviruses) and common autoinflammatory syndromes (negative genetic testing for MEFV, MVK, TNFRSF1A, NLRP3, NLRP12). CSF analysis consistently showed >1000 polymorphonuclear leukocytes/mm³. At age 68, the patient developed severe hemolysis with hemoglobin declining to 8.2 g/dL, LDH elevated to 3004 IU/L, hemoglobinuria (brownish urine), and acute renal failure (creatinine increased from 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL) with hemosiderin deposition in renal tubules, requiring temporary hemodialysis for one month. Flow cytometric analysis revealed deficiency of CD55 and CD59 (GPI-anchored proteins) on both erythrocytes and granulocytes, confirming the diagnosis of PNH. Treatment with eculizumab (complement inhibitor) resulted in complete resolution of all symptoms including urticaria, arthralgia, headache, and hemolysis, with remission sustained for 3 years. The recurrent aseptic meningitis with neutrophilic CSF infiltration represents a complement-mediated manifestation of PNH.

final.final_diagnosis: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) with recurrent aseptic meningitis
final.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with 121 episodes of recurrent aseptic meningitis over 18 years, beginning at age 53. He had a prior history of recurrent urticaria and arthralgia since age 30. Extensive initial workup ruled out infectious etiologies (negative bacterial, fungal, mycobacterial cultures; negative PCR for herpesviruses and enteroviruses) and common autoinflammatory syndromes (negative genetic testing for MEFV, MVK, TNFRSF1A, NLRP3, NLRP12). CSF analysis consistently showed >1000 polymorphonuclear leukocytes/mm³. At age 68, the patient developed severe hemolysis with hemoglobin declining to 8.2 g/dL, LDH elevated to 3004 IU/L, hemoglobinuria (brownish urine), and acute renal failure (creatinine increased from 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL) with hemosiderin deposition in renal tubules, requiring temporary hemodialysis for one month. Flow cytometric analysis revealed deficiency of CD55 and CD59 (GPI-anchored proteins) on both erythrocytes and granulocytes, confirming the diagnosis of PNH. Treatment with eculizumab (complement inhibitor) resulted in complete resolution of all symptoms including urticaria, arthralgia, headache, and hemolysis, with remission sustained for 3 years. The recurrent aseptic meningitis with neutrophilic CSF infiltration represents a complement-mediated manifestation of PNH.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: 121 episodes of recurrent aseptic meningitis over 18 years starting at age 53
Recurrent urticaria and arthralgia since age 30, preceding meningitis onset
CSF with >1000 polymorphonuclear leukocytes/mm³, negative for bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria, herpesviruses, and enteroviruses
Urticarial biopsy showed neutrophil infiltration
Genetic testing negative for MEFV, MVK, TNFRSF1A, NLRP3, NLRP12
At age 68: severe hemolysis with hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL and LDH 3004 IU/L
Hemoglobinuria (brownish urine) and altered consciousness during meningitis episodes
Acute renal failure with creatinine increase from 2.8 to 8.65 mg/dL and hemosiderin deposition in renal tubules
Required temporary hemodialysis for one month
Flow cytometry confirmed deficiency of CD55 and CD59 (GPI-anchored proteins) on erythrocytes and granulocytes
Diagnosed with PNH in addition to recurrent meningitis
All symptoms (urticaria, arthralgia, headache, hemolysis) completely disappeared with eculizumab therapy
Remission sustained for 3 years on eculizumab

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative cultures and PCR testing; recurrent episodes over 18 years without pathogenic organism identification
Negative genetic testing for MEFV; colchicine trial without evidence of benefit
Negative genetic testing for NLRP3 and NLRP12

remaining_uncertainties: Whether PNH was present but unrecognized during the first 15 years of meningitis episodes (age 53-68), or whether it manifested acutely at age 68
Specific meningitis episode frequency and clinical course during the 3-year remission period on eculizumab (whether meningitis episodes completely ceased or continued at reduced frequency)
Complete hemolysis laboratory panel during acute hemolytic episode at age 68 (haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin, reticulocyte count, hematocrit)
Whether thrombotic events occurred during the course of PNH
Evidence of subclinical hemolysis or complement activation during the first 15 years of meningitis before age 68

evaluation.known_final_diagnosis: he was diagnosed with PNH in addition to recurrent meningitis
